title: Trump Fires FTC Democratic Commissioners Bedoya and Slaughter
description_short: Trump Fires FTC Democratic Commissioners Bedoya and Slaughter
description_medium: On March 18, 2025, Donald Trump removed the Federal Trade Commission’s two Democratic commissioners, Alvaro Bedoya and Rebecca Kelly Slaughter. Both challenged the dismissals in court. In July, a federal judge ruled Slaughter’s removal unlawful, finding that statutory protections for FTC commissioners remained constitutional. The firings changed the agency’s partisan balance and raised questions about its independence in antitrust and consumer-protection enforcement.
description_long: Donald Trump fired Federal Trade Commission commissioners Alvaro Bedoya and Rebecca Kelly Slaughter on March 18, 2025. Both commissioners said the removals were unlawful and filed suit. The dismissals removed the two Democratic members from the five-person commission, changing the agency’s balance and giving the administration greater influence over antitrust and consumer-protection decisions. On July 17, U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan ruled that Slaughter’s removal violated statutory protections for FTC commissioners. The judge held that the for-cause protections remained constitutional under longstanding Supreme Court precedent. That ruling directly addressed Slaughter’s dismissal; it did not itself resolve every issue concerning Bedoya’s separate case. The episode raised questions about the president’s authority to remove independent-agency commissioners and the FTC’s ability to operate apart from short-term political control. The supplied account notes that the commission’s oversight could affect companies with business before the agency, including firms associated with Elon Musk. The record does not establish that any specific enforcement matter was altered because of the dismissals. It documents the firings, litigation and judicial ruling, while showing how a personnel decision can affect the composition and perceived independence of a regulator.

title: Asylum System Dismantled: CBP One Killed, Border Declared Closed Day One
description_short: Asylum System Dismantled: CBP One Killed, Border Declared Closed Day One
description_medium: On January 20, 2025, the CBP One appointment app stopped accepting asylum appointments after Donald Trump took office, ending a process that had allowed up to 1,450 people a day to schedule border appointments. Trump also issued an order declaring an invasion and restricting access to asylum procedures. The changes left people waiting in Mexican border cities without the appointments they had secured; later transfers to third countries raised further concerns.
description_long: Within minutes of Donald Trump’s inauguration on January 20, 2025, the CBP One app was shut down. The app had allowed as many as 1,450 migrants each day to schedule appointments to seek asylum at the border and had processed more than 900,000 entrants since 2023. Its closure stranded thousands of people who had been waiting in Mexican border cities for appointments. Trump also issued an executive order declaring an “invasion” at the southern border and suspending asylum processing, arguing that emergency powers allowed the government to bar claims. The legality of that approach was disputed, and the supplied account says the order went beyond statutory authority. The administration also paused the refugee resettlement program for four months. The loss of the appointment system and suspension of asylum procedures sharply reduced legal routes available to people seeking protection. In June, the United States reached Safe Third Country agreements with Guatemala and Honduras that allowed transfer of some asylum seekers to those countries. The episode is significant because it combined an immediate technology shutdown with changes to asylum policy, leaving people who had followed the prior process without their scheduled appointments and creating uncertainty about access to protection.

title: DOGE Seeks Access to IRS Taxpayer Data on All Americans
description_short: DOGE Seeks Access to IRS Taxpayer Data on All Americans
description_medium: In February 2025, the Department of Government Efficiency sought access to the IRS’s Integrated Data Retrieval System, which contains highly sensitive taxpayer information. IRS sources said DOGE engineer Gavin Kliger was expected to receive access, while Senators Ron Wyden and Elizabeth Warren warned about the proposal. The supplied account says DOGE already had access to data at other agencies; privacy advocates questioned the legal basis and safeguards for consolidating those records.
description_long: In February 2025, Elon Musk's Department of Government Efficiency sought access to the IRS's Integrated Data Retrieval System — a heavily protected database containing the financial records, tax returns, Social Security numbers, bank account details, and employment information of every taxpayer, business, and nonprofit in the country. DOGE software engineer Gavin Kliger was set to be granted access imminently, according to IRS sources. Democratic Senators Ron Wyden and Elizabeth Warren wrote to the acting IRS Commissioner calling the proposal weaponization of taxpayer data. The move came alongside DOGE already having penetrated Treasury Department payment systems, Social Security Administration records, and at least seven other major agency databases. A Washington Post investigation found DOGE had secured access to competitors' trade secrets and nonpublic regulatory data at those agencies. Privacy advocates warned the consolidation of data from multiple agencies in DOGE's hands had no legal precedent.

title: Trump DOJ Indicts James Comey and Letitia James on Political Charges
description_short: Trump DOJ Indicts James Comey and Letitia James on Political Charges
description_medium: In September and October 2025, federal grand juries indicted former FBI Director James Comey and New York Attorney General Letitia James after Donald Trump publicly called for action against political adversaries. The indictments were later dismissed when a judge ruled that prosecutor Lindsey Halligan had been unlawfully appointed and lacked authority to bring the cases. The sequence raised concerns about political pressure on prosecutors and the independence of federal law enforcement.
description_long: On September 25, 2025, a federal grand jury indicted former FBI Director James Comey on two charges of lying to Congress, in a case filed days after Trump publicly appeared to demand prosecution of longtime foes. On October 9, 2025, a Trump-handpicked prosecutor named Lindsey Halligan — an insurance lawyer with zero prior prosecutorial experience who was previously part of Trump's personal legal team — secured an indictment of New York Attorney General Letitia James on bank fraud charges related to a home purchase, after Trump publicly called for her prosecution on Truth Social. The original U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia resigned under pressure to prosecute James. On November 24, 2025, a federal judge dismissed both indictments, ruling that Halligan had been illegally appointed and lacked authority to bring charges. The episode was described by the New York Times as the most direct intervention in the justice system since the Nixon era.

title: Pride Flags Banned from All U.S. Embassies and Federal Sites
description_short: Pride Flags Banned from All U.S. Embassies and Federal Sites
description_medium: The supplied record says Secretary of State Marco Rubio issued a January 2025 “One Flag Policy” barring Pride and other non-U.S. flags at diplomatic posts and domestic federal sites. The only linked article is from March 2024 and covers a proposed funding-bill restriction at embassies, not the described 2025 cable or its extension to domestic buildings. A source documenting the 2025 policy’s text and scope is needed before this record can be marked complete.
description_long: On January 21, 2025, Secretary of State Marco Rubio issued a 'One Flag Policy' cable to all U.S. diplomatic posts immediately prohibiting the display of any flag other than the American flag at all U.S. facilities domestic and abroad, with the only exceptions being the POW/MIA flag and the Wrongful Detainees Flag. The policy explicitly targeted pride and Black Lives Matter flags that had flown at Biden-era embassies, including the U.S. Embassy in Nassau during Pride Month 2021 and U.S. facilities in Brazil. Employees who violate the policy face disciplinary action up to and including termination or contract cancellation. The White House highlighted the policy in a news release listing actions taken in Trump's first 100 hours. The ban extended to all domestic federal buildings and official U.S. government content, effectively signaling to LGBTQ foreign nationals that American diplomatic missions would no longer publicly affirm their equality. Pride flags had first been permitted at U.S. embassies under the Obama administration and were banned during Trump's first term starting in 2019.

title: Elon Musk Runs DOGE While His Companies Collect $38 Billion in Government Contracts
description_short: Elon Musk Runs DOGE While His Companies Collect $38 Billion in Government Contracts
description_medium: Donald Trump placed Elon Musk in a leadership role at the Department of Government Efficiency while Musk’s companies had received an estimated $38 billion in government contracts, subsidies, loans and tax credits. DOGE sought cuts at agencies that also funded or regulated those businesses, including NASA and the Defense Department. The White House said Musk was a special government employee; lawmakers and ethics observers raised concerns about conflicts of interest and the absence of a public waiver.
description_long: Trump appointed Elon Musk — the world's wealthiest individual and a contractor whose companies SpaceX, Tesla, and Starlink had received a reported $38 billion in government funds — as the de facto head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), tasked with cutting federal spending at the very agencies that oversaw, funded, and regulated his business interests. The White House acknowledged in February 2025 that Musk was serving as a special government employee with no public conflict-of-interest waiver, while Musk claimed he would self-recuse from relevant matters. Democratic lawmakers wrote in May 2025 to Defense Secretary Hegseth and NASA Acting Administrator Petro specifically flagging that Musk's dual role as SpaceX CEO and DOGE lead created an inherent conflict of interest since SpaceX was a large government contractor at NASA and DoD. Walter Shaub, former director of the Office of Government Ethics, stated flatly: A conflict of interest waiver for Musk could not be justified. Elon Musk is the world's richest individual who is a government contractor. Despite these warnings, Starlink was simultaneously being expanded across federal agencies, and SpaceX won additional NASA and Pentagon contracts during the same period Musk wielded DOGE authority over the agencies awarding them.

title: Federal Judge War - 'Judicial Tyranny' Attacks and Constitutional Crisis
description_short: Federal Judge War - 'Judicial Tyranny' Attacks and Constitutional Crisis
description_medium: From May through August 2025, Donald Trump and administration officials criticized federal judges whose rulings blocked parts of the administration’s agenda. Stephen Miller posted judges’ photographs and biographies, while officials sued courts and filed complaints against Chief Judge James Boasberg. Judges warned that public attacks and noncompliance could weaken judicial independence. The administration called some rulings “judicial tyranny”; the dispute raised separation-of-powers concerns.
description_long: Donald Trump escalated his war against federal judges to unprecedented levels, with his administration declaring 'We are living under a judicial tyranny' while systematically attacking, suing, and attempting to intimidate judges whose rulings constrained his authoritarian agenda. Trump advisor Stephen Miller publicly posted images and biographies of three judges who ruled against Trump's tariff authority, calling them tyrannical despite being appointed by Reagan, Obama, and Trump himself. The administration filed lawsuits against entire federal courts and lodged judicial misconduct complaints against Chief Judge James Boasberg of the influential DC District Court, representing the first time a president has sued judges for ruling against him. Attorney General Pam Bondi described some judges as 'deranged' while the administration systematically evaded court orders blocking its agenda, with current and former federal judges warning the conflict could escalate into a constitutional crisis. At rallies, Trump declared that 'communist radical-left judges' were trying to 'take away the powers given to the president,' positioning judges as enemies of democracy rather than defenders of constitutional law. The administration's defiance of court orders, particularly on immigration, created what CNN described as an unprecedented situation where 'the courts are helpless' against executive branch evasion. Former and current federal judges speaking anonymously warned that Trump was 'attempting to intimidate, threaten, and overpower the courts in unprecedented ways.'

title: ICE Arrests Parishioner on Catholic Church Grounds in Inland Empire
description_short: ICE Arrests Parishioner on Catholic Church Grounds in Inland Empire
description_medium: On June 20, 2025, immigration agents detained a longtime parishioner who was landscaping on the grounds of Our Lady of Lourdes Church in Montclair, California, and pursued men onto the parking lot of nearby St. Adelaide Parish. The Diocese of San Bernardino criticized the operations as disregarding due process and dignity; DHS disputed some characterizations. The incidents followed a policy change ending protections for sensitive locations and drew responses from clergy and state legislators.
description_long: On June 20, 2025 — World Refugee Day — federal immigration agents conducted enforcement operations on the grounds of two Catholic churches in San Bernardino County, California, marking a stark application of Trump's January 21 order eliminating protections for sensitive locations. At Our Lady of Lourdes Church in Montclair, agents detained a longtime parishioner who was doing landscaping work on church property. According to the Roman Catholic Diocese of San Bernardino, the man was a parishioner whose family was involved in the church ministry. In a separate incident the same day, agents chased several men onto the parking lot of St. Adelaide Parish in Highland. DHS Assistant Secretary Tricia McLaughlin disputed characterizations of the events. Bishop Alberto Rojas of the Diocese of San Bernardino wrote to parishioners that authorities are now seizing brothers and sisters indiscriminately, without respect for their right to due process and their dignity as children of God, calling the raids not of the Gospel of Jesus Christ. The newly appointed Bishop of the Diocese of San Diego, Michael Pham — himself a Vietnamese refugee who came to the US in 1981 — joined clergy outside the San Diego federal building the same day to witness immigration proceedings. Six California Republican state legislators signed a letter asking Trump to focus only on violent criminals, saying ICE raids at farms, churches, and workplaces were harming the communities we represent.

title: Federal Scientific Data Manipulation - Climate Research Falsification and Evidence Suppression
description_short: Federal Scientific Data Manipulation - Climate Research Falsification and Evidence Suppression
description_medium: The existing long description alleges that federal agencies falsified climate data, suppressed research and dismissed scientists who resisted. The linked American Public Health Association page addresses Project 2025 as a policy threat, but the provided source does not document the specific completed acts alleged here, such as NOAA altering temperature records or EPA suppressing toxicity studies. Evidence tying those claims to implemented agency actions is needed before this entry can be marked complete.
description_long: Donald Trump implemented systematic manipulation of federal scientific data by requiring agencies to falsify climate research, suppress environmental findings, and publish altered datasets that supported fossil fuel industry interests while eliminating scientific integrity protections that had prevented political interference with research evidence and factual information. The comprehensive data manipulation represented Trump's transformation of federal science agencies from objective research institutions into propaganda operations that produced false information designed to justify environmental deregulation and climate science denial rather than providing accurate scientific assessment for policy decisions. The scientific falsification included directing NOAA to alter temperature records, EPA to suppress toxicity studies, and other agencies to modify research conclusions that conflicted with administration ideology while terminating scientists who refused to participate in data manipulation or evidence suppression. Trump's research manipulation violated scientific integrity principles by requiring federal scientists to produce false data while eliminating whistleblower protections for researchers who exposed scientific misconduct, creating systems where political loyalty determined research conclusions rather than scientific evidence and methodology. The data falsification created what researchers called 'complete corruption of federal science' where agencies published manipulated information designed to serve political agenda rather than inform public policy through accurate scientific assessment, effectively ending government's role in providing objective information about environmental and health threats. The scientific manipulation represented Project 2025's vision of research controlled by political ideology rather than scientific method, transforming federal agencies from evidence-based institutions into propaganda operations that prioritized conservative political messaging over factual accuracy and public protection through reliable scientific information.

title: Voice of America and USAGM Media Closure - International Broadcasting Propaganda Transformation
description_short: Voice of America and USAGM Media Closure - International Broadcasting Propaganda Transformation
description_medium: The existing long description says the administration eliminated the U.S. Agency for Global Media and converted its outlets into propaganda services. The supplied links discuss Project 2025 and press-freedom risks, but were not accessible and do not, from their titles, document the specific 2025 shutdown actions or current status of VOA, RFE/RL and RFA. A source showing what was actually closed, suspended or retained is needed to support this account.
description_long: Donald Trump implemented Project 2025's systematic destruction of independent international media by eliminating the US Agency for Global Media (USAGM) that operated Voice of America, Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty, and Radio Free Asia, while transforming remaining outlets into 'propaganda outlets' that promoted administration ideology rather than factual journalism to global audiences. The comprehensive media elimination represented Trump's strategy to end 'pillars of U.S. international broadcasting' including Voice of America - 'the oldest U.S. international news broadcaster dating back to 1942' - that had provided 'factual, uncensored news reporting' in authoritarian countries where independent journalism faced persecution and censorship. The international broadcasting destruction included gutting the 'independent Open Technology Fund' that fought digital surveillance and internet censorship worldwide, while eliminating Corporation for Public Broadcasting funding unless outlets were 'reformed' to represent Project 2025's 'approved ideological slant' that prevented criticism of U.S. government policies. Trump's media targeting violated press freedom principles by transforming independent journalism into government propaganda operations, ending editorial independence that had maintained credibility with international audiences who relied on U.S. media for accurate information about global events and American democracy. The broadcasting elimination created what press freedom advocates called abandonment of America's commitment to independent journalism and democratic values, ending media services that had historically provided uncensored news to people living under authoritarian regimes while promoting democratic principles through factual reporting. The Voice of America destruction represented Project 2025's vision of international communication controlled by government ideology rather than journalistic integrity, transforming U.S. international broadcasting from independent news source into state propaganda system that served political agenda rather than democratic values and press freedom principles.
